zh.title: CEH M01｜C17–C24：安全控制與資料清理

sections.heading: 核心結論：資訊安全不是裝了多少防護工具，而是能否有效控制風險，並在資料生命週期結束時確實消除暴露風險

body.text: CEH v13 · M01-06 安全控制與縱深防禦 · 8 個核心觀念
這一單元有兩個核心問題：
第一，如何保護仍在使用的系統與資料？ 我們需要理解 Security Controls（安全控制），包括實體控制、技術控制、防火牆、防毒軟體與加密。
第二，當資料不再需要時，如何確保資料不會被還原？ 這涉及 Media Sanitization（媒體資料清理）、Purge、一般檔案刪除、儲存媒體回收及資料保存政策。
這兩個問題其實是同一件事的不同階段：

body.name: lifecyclecontrols
body.caption: 資料生命週期與清理
body.description: 清理方法依資料風險、媒體能力與驗證結果選擇。

items.title: 使用中的資料
items.body: 防止未授權存取、竄改與服務中斷。

items.title: 儲存、備份與封存
items.body: 控制誰可以存取、如何保存、保存多久。

items.title: 生命週期終點
items.body: 選擇 Clear、Purge、Destroy 等適當處置。

items.title: 驗證與證據
items.body: 驗證清理結果並保存證據，確保後續再利用、報廢或委外回收符合風險要求。

body.text: 特別重要的是，NIST 已於 2025 年 9 月 26 日正式發布 SP 800-88 Revision 2，取代 2014 年的 Revision 1。新版更重視企業整體媒體清理制度、清理方法的可信度及驗證，而不是只教你操作某種刪除工具。
因此，本次教學將保留 CEH 題目中的術語，同時使用現行 NIST 標準解釋它們的真正技術意義。

sections.heading: 一、完整知識地圖：C17–C24

body.text: 本次供稿將本單元八個觀念歸在 M01-06。其中 C17–C21 屬於安全控制分類及具體控制，C22–C24 則聚焦資料清理與不同資料處置行為的辨析。供稿所引用的課程附件將後三個觀念標示為待核子項；本文不據此宣稱已有獨立正式課次。

rows: 安全控制應如何分類與選擇？
實體保全與環境保護能防止什麼？
防火牆如何控制網路流量？
防毒軟體如何辨識及阻擋惡意程式？
加密能保護哪些安全性質？
如何清理資料，使進階復原方法不可行？
刪除檔案為什麼不等於清除實際資料？
硬體回收、資料封存與資料清理有何不同？

body.text: 我們仍採用三種真實產業的工程場景：臺灣半導體製造、美國矽谷雲端科技業，以及金管會監理下的臺灣金融機構；以 NIST、OWASP 和 MITRE ATT&CK 建立技術解釋，再用適用法律、產業標準與自律規範確認實務要求。

sections.heading: 二、C17｜Security Controls：安全控制到底是什麼？

body.text: 1. 白話理解：控制風險，而不是消滅所有風險
假設你負責一座先進晶圓廠的資安管理。
公司擔心三件事：

items: 外部攻擊者從網路入侵製造管理系統。
未授權人員進入設備機房。
報廢硬碟中的製程資料被第三方還原。

body.text: 你會怎麼辦？
對第一件事，可以設置防火牆、網路區隔及存取控制；第二件事需要門禁與保全；第三件事則需要資料清理及報廢管理。
這些都是 Security Controls（安全控制）。
它們不一定是軟體，也可能是人員、政策、設備、工作流程或技術機制。
NIST SP 800-53 Rev. 5 的安全控制目錄包括 Access Control（AC）、Physical and Environmental Protection（PE）、System and Communications Protection（SC）、Media Protection（MP）等控制家族。其維護版本已更新至 Release 5.2.0。
2. 安全控制必須同時理解三個分類維度
這是本章第一個核心觀念。

body.name: controlaxes
body.caption: 控制措施的三個分類軸
body.description: 三個軸可同時描述同一項控制，彼此不是先後步驟。 一項控制可能同時具有預防、偵測及其他作用；這些軸不是互斥分類。

items.title: A｜實作形式
items.body: Administrative：政策、制度、人員與程序／Technical：軟體、系統、網路與密碼學／Physical：門禁、保全、機房與實體設備

items.title: B｜控制功能
items.body: Preventive｜預防：降低事件發生機會／Detective｜偵測：發現事件或異常／Corrective｜矯正：修正已發現的問題／Recovery｜復原：恢復必要能力／Deterrent｜嚇阻：降低行為動機／Compensating｜補償：替代或補足其他控制

items.title: C｜保護目標
items.body: Confidentiality（機密性）、Integrity（完整性）、Availability（可用性），以及適用情境下的身分、可追溯性和隱私等要求。

body.text: 注意：這些維度可以交叉組合，並不是三套互相排斥的分類。一個控制也可能同時具有預防、偵測和其他作用。
3. 一個控制可以擁有多種功能

rows: 保護資料機密性；搭配適當模式可驗證完整性

body.text: 最後一列很重要。安全控制要依據實際機制分類。
使用加密清除金鑰，是邏輯／技術操作；將儲存晶片實體粉碎，則屬實體處置。兩者都可能用於媒體資料清理，但不代表使用相同的控制形式。
4. Defense in Depth：為什麼需要多層控制？
假設半導體公司只部署了防火牆。
如果內部員工直接將機密資料複製到隨身碟，防火牆可能根本看不到這個行為。
再假設公司只有機房保全。
如果攻擊者透過合法開放的 HTTPS 服務利用 API 弱點，保全也無法直接阻止。
所以，我們需要縱深防禦（Defense in Depth）。

body.name: defenselayers
body.caption: 四層縱深防禦
body.description: 外層包覆內層，多層控制共同保護核心資產。 多層防禦旨在避免單一控制失效就造成不可接受的後果；各控制仍須分別驗證有效性。

items.title: 實體與環境
items.body: 門禁、機房與環境保護

items.title: 網路區隔與流量
items.body: 網段、邊界與流量控制

items.title: 端點與身分
items.body: 端點防護、帳號與權限管理

items.title: 關鍵資料與系統
items.body: 加密、驗證、備份與完整性

body.text: C17 核心： 分類安全控制時，先問它如何實施，再問它如何發揮作用，最後問它保護哪一項安全目標。

sections.heading: 三、C18｜Physical Controls：為什麼保全人員是資訊安全控制？

body.text: 1. 網路再安全，實體資產仍可能遭到接觸
假設一家銀行擁有非常安全的資料庫。
系統有防火牆、加密及多因素驗證。
但機房門沒有上鎖，外部訪客可以直接進入，拿走備份媒體或接觸伺服器。
這時問題不是缺少加密演算法，而是缺少 Physical Controls。
實體安全控制就是透過人員、設施與實體機制，防止未經授權的人接觸重要資產。
2. 為什麼 Security Guard 屬於 Physical Control？
保全人員透過現場身分確認、巡邏、監控與進出管制，限制實體空間的存取。
NIST SP 800-53 Rev. 5 的 PE-3（Physical Access Control）明確將 guards 納入設施進出控制的實施方式；PE-6（Monitoring Physical Access）則規範實體存取監控與事件回應。
注意：保全人員當然也是「人員」，但在此分類中，他執行的主要控制是實體安全，而不是 Administrative Control。
這是 CEH 非常容易考的概念。
3. 臺灣半導體實務：機房與製造設備區域
假設某晶圓廠有三種空間：

rows: 限制授權人員、機櫃上鎖、存取紀錄
製造控制設備、設備維修介面
維修人員授權、設備實體存取管制、現場安全程序

body.text: 這是依據資產風險所設計的示例。
NIST SP 800-82 Rev. 3 強調，OT 系統的安全控制必須考慮實體製程、安全性與可用性之間的關係。
因此，在製造設備環境，門禁與緊急疏散設計也必須協調，不能讓資安控制阻礙人員安全。
4. 與臺灣金融監理的關係
《金融控股公司及銀行業內部控制及稽核制度實施辦法》第 12 條要求內部控制涵蓋資訊管理及客戶資料保密，第 25 條要求資訊安全制度維持機密性、完整性與可用性。
實體門禁、訪客管理與機房保護可以作為金融機構實現這些目標的控制措施，但不能將上述條文解讀成「每一家銀行依法必須採用同一種保全人員配置」。
C18 核心： Security Guard、門禁、圍籬與機櫃鎖，主要屬於 Physical Security Controls；防火牆與加密則屬於 Technical Controls。

sections.heading: 四、C19｜Firewall：防火牆在保護什麼？

body.text: 1. 防火牆就是網路交通的管制站
假設一座晶圓廠有兩個網路：

items: IT Network：企業辦公與一般資訊系統。
OT Network：製造設備與工廠控制系統。

body.text: 公司不希望辦公電腦可以任意連線到製造設備。
因此，在兩個網路之間建立防火牆。

body.name: firewallpolicy
body.caption: IT／OT 防火牆邊界
body.description: 只有核准且符合政策的流量能通過；Deny 表示阻擋。

items.title: IT 網路
items.body: 企業辦公端點與一般資訊系統。

items.title: 防火牆
items.body: 檢查來源、目的與服務規則

items.title: OT 網路
items.body: 製造設備與工廠作業控制系統。

items.title: Allow｜核准管理
items.body: 符合規則的管理連線允許通過。

items.title: Deny｜未授權直連
items.body: 阻擋未經核准的直接連線。

body.text: 防火牆會依照規則與流量特徵，判斷哪些網路連線允許通過。
常見的判斷資訊包括來源／目的 IP、通訊協定、連接埠及連線狀態。較進階產品還會檢查應用層流量。
NIST SP 800-53 的 SC-7（Boundary Protection）屬於系統邊界防護的重要控制；在 OT 環境可結合 NIST SP 800-82 Rev. 3 進行網路區隔設計。
2. 防火牆不是萬能的
想像美國矽谷一家 SaaS 公司，已經允許使用者透過 HTTPS 存取 API。
攻擊者使用正常網路連線，卻透過 API 的權限驗證缺陷讀取其他使用者的資料。
防火牆可能允許 HTTPS 通過，因為連線本身符合網路政策。
真正的問題在於應用程式的授權邏輯。
因此還需要：

items: Network Firewall：保護網路與連線邊界。
WAF（Web Application Firewall）：檢查 HTTP 請求中的可疑模式。
Application Authorization：由後端程式檢查使用者對特定資料或功能的權限。

body.text: OWASP WSTG 指出，WAF 可以協助阻擋 SQL Injection 或 XSS 等常見攻擊，但對存取控制與業務邏輯問題的保護能力有限。
3. 工程上如何驗證防火牆？
不能只問：「有沒有裝防火牆？」
應該問：

items: 哪些連線應該被允許？哪些應該被拒絕？
實際規則是否符合最小必要存取？
是否存在可繞過預期網路路徑的連線？
規則是否定期檢查，變更是否留下紀錄？
發現異常連線時，是否有監控與處置機制？

body.text: C19 核心：Firewall 是 Technical Control，主要提供網路流量的預防性管制，也可以提供監控與紀錄；它不能取代應用程式內部授權。

sections.heading: 五、C20｜Antivirus：防毒軟體究竟如何知道程式有問題？

body.text: 1. 防毒不是只有比對病毒名稱
假設半導體設備維修人員將一個 USB 裝置接到維修電腦。
USB 裡有一個看似正常的工具程式，但實際上包含惡意程式。
防毒軟體可能透過數種方式發現問題。

rows: 比對已知惡意程式特徵
未知變種可能沒有相符特徵
分析可疑程式結構或行為特徵
觀察執行時的可疑行為
惡意行為可能已部分發生
蒐集端點活動、調查並回應事件
需要正確部署、權限與持續監控

body.text: 這些機制可能共存於同一產品。
NIST SP 800-53 的 SI-3（Malicious Code Protection）是惡意程式防護的對應控制。
2. 半導體產業的特殊需求：安全更新可能影響設備
一般員工電腦可能採用較頻繁的安全更新。
但如果一台製造設備使用經過高度驗證的控制軟體，更新端點防護元件可能影響設備驅動程式、效能或可用性。
因此，不能把一般辦公電腦的更新方法，毫無調整地套用在所有製造設備上。
SEMI 產業標準：
SEMI E187《Specification for Cybersecurity of Fab Equipment》建立半導體製造設備的基礎資安要求，包含作業系統、網路安全、端點防護與日誌等面向。
SEMI E188《Specification for Malware Free Equipment Integration》則專注於設備交付與支援過程中，降低惡意程式進入製造環境或傳播的風險。
兩者的定位不同：E187 側重設備資安基線，E188 側重設備整合與支援過程的惡意程式傳播防範。
值得注意的是，SEMI 於 2026 年公布了 E187 分級安全架構的重大修訂方向；該修訂計畫不能直接視為所有現有設備都已適用的新規定。
3. 防毒不是資料清理工具
這一點要和 C22–C24 連起來理解。
假設銀行有一台準備報廢的伺服器，已安裝最新版本防毒軟體，也沒有檢出病毒。
這並不代表伺服器中的客戶資料已經安全清除。
因為：
Antivirus 管理惡意程式風險；Media Sanitization 管理殘留資料的機密性風險。
前者不能取代後者。
C20 核心：防毒軟體屬 Technical Control，可能具有預防、偵測及部分回應功能；即使沒有檢出惡意程式，也不代表系統不存在其他安全風險。

sections.heading: 六、C21｜Encryption：加密能解決什麼？又不能解決什麼？

body.text: 1. 加密的目的，是讓未持有必要金鑰者難以理解資料
假設一家矽谷科技公司在雲端儲存客戶的重要商業資料。
資料若以明文儲存，儲存設備遭到未授權存取時，內容可能直接暴露。
若使用適當的加密設計，未持有解密金鑰者即使取得密文，也難以還原內容。
最基本的加密模型：
C = E_K(P)
P = D_K(C)
其中：

items: P：Plaintext（明文）。
C：Ciphertext（密文）。
K：加密與解密所需的金鑰（對稱加密）。
E、D：加密及解密演算法。

body.text: 2. 加密主要保護機密性，但可以結合完整性保護
這是另一個容易誤解的地方。
如果只使用不提供驗證能力的加密模式，加密本身不一定能防止攻擊者不被察覺地修改密文。
現代系統常採用 Authenticated Encryption with Associated Data（AEAD），例如 AES-GCM。
AEAD 可以同時提供機密性與資料完整性驗證；但它不會自動解決業務授權、金鑰遭竊或使用者身分歸屬等問題。
OWASP《Cryptographic Storage Cheat Sheet》建議使用成熟的密碼學函式庫、適當演算法及安全的金鑰管理方法，而不是自行發明加密機制。
3. 三種資料狀態，需要不同的保護設計

rows: 磁碟、資料庫或物件層級加密
記憶體與執行環境保護；特定情況使用機密運算

body.text: 4. 為什麼金鑰管理比想像中重要？
假設半導體公司把客戶設計檔案全部加密，卻把解密金鑰寫在同一台伺服器的公開設定檔中。
攻擊者取得檔案時，也取得金鑰。
結果就是：雖然有加密，卻未必達到預期保護效果。
OWASP 建議依系統設計妥善管理金鑰產生、儲存、輪替、停用與銷毀，並在適合的架構中將資料加密金鑰（DEK）與金鑰加密金鑰（KEK）分層管理。
更深一層的問題是：
如果資料已經加密，那麼刪掉解密金鑰，是不是就等同於清除資料？
這正是下一個 C22 的核心。答案取決於金鑰、加密實作、資料副本及媒體清理條件，不能只根據「有加密」就作出判斷。

sections.heading: 七、C22｜Purge：真正的資料清理是什麼？

body.text: 這是整個 C17–C24 中，技術細節最值得深入理解的部分。
1. 白話理解：看不到資料，不代表資料不存在
假設臺灣半導體公司準備將一台使用五年的伺服器轉交設備回收商。
IT 人員說：
「我已經把硬碟格式化，所有檔案都不見了。」
這是否代表硬碟已經安全？
不一定。
因為檔案是否出現在作業系統中，以及儲存媒體是否還留有可還原的資料，是兩件不同的事。
我們真正要考慮的是：
假設下一位持有這個儲存媒體的人具有專業鑑識設備、時間與技術能力，他是否仍能還原原本的機密資料？
這是 Media Sanitization 要處理的問題。
2. NIST SP 800-88 Rev. 2：Clear、Purge、Destroy 三種方法
NIST SP 800-88 Rev. 2 第 3.1 節正式定義三種資料清理方法。

body.name: sanitizationmethods
body.caption: Clear／Purge／Destroy 比較
body.description: 三種方法依資料敏感性、媒體及後續用途選擇，並非必須依序執行。

items.title: Clear｜§3.1.1
items.body: 目標：抵抗簡單、非侵入式的資料復原。針對使用者可存取的儲存區域，採用適當的邏輯清理技術。例：對適合的媒體，透過標準讀寫介面覆寫使用者可定址的資料區域。

items.title: Purge｜§3.1.2
items.body: 目標：使先進實驗室復原技術也無法可行地還原目標資料。使用適合媒體的邏輯或實體技術，並保留媒體可能再次使用的能力。例：符合條件的裝置清理指令、Cryptographic Erase。

items.title: Destroy｜§3.1.3
items.body: 目標：使資料無法以先進實驗室技術可行地復原，並讓媒體失去儲存功能。使用符合媒體特性的實體破壞程序。例：適當規格的媒體粉碎、解體或其他核准的銷毀技術。

rows: 技術能達到較高保護程度
清理結果符合銷毀要求

body.text: 這裡的差別是威脅模型與可達成的清理保證，不是簡單地比較「覆寫一次、三次或七次」。
新版 NIST 特別要求清理技術與實際媒體特性相符，並參照 IEEE 2883、相關 NSA 規格或組織核准的標準。
3. 為什麼 Purge 不能理解成數學上的「永遠不可能復原」？
本次供稿特別標示了原題用語的這項疑義。
供稿轉述原題使用 impossible even with laboratory-grade tools 這類過於絕對的語句；此處未獨立核對原題全文。標準中的概念是：在指定的技術與資源條件下，使復原資料不可行。
這裡應區分：

items: Logical impossibility： 邏輯上根本不可能。
Computational infeasibility： 在實際可用的時間、資源與技術能力下，無法可行地完成。
Operational assurance： 依照可信程序執行，並具有足夠證據支持清理結果。

body.text: NIST 採用的是風險與能力導向的判準，不是宣稱任何媒體都能取得不受未來技術影響的絕對保證。
4. 為什麼傳統覆寫方法不適合直接套用在所有 SSD？
先了解 HDD 與 SSD 的差異。
傳統 HDD 主要透過磁性方式儲存資料。
SSD 則使用快閃記憶體，並透過控制器管理實際資料位置、磨耗平均化（Wear Leveling）及備用儲存區域（Overprovisioning）。
因此，當作業系統要求寫入某個邏輯位址時，SSD 控制器可能把資料寫到另一個實體位置，而不是直接覆蓋原本的儲存單元。

body.name: ssdremapping
body.caption: SSD 邏輯覆寫與 FTL 重新映射
body.description: 舊 Page A 與新 Page B 是重新映射後並存的狀態，不是 A 再寫入 B 的時間步驟。 實際行為取決於 SSD 控制器、韌體和儲存技術，不代表每次覆寫都會產生完全相同的結果。

items.title: 作業系統
items.body: 要求覆寫邏輯區塊 LBA 100。

items.title: SSD 控制器／FTL
items.body: 將邏輯位址映射至實體快閃記憶體。

items.title: 舊 Page A
items.body: 原本的實體儲存頁面：舊資料可能尚未被實體抹除。

items.title: 新 Page B
items.body: 新的實體儲存頁面：新資料寫入完成。

body.text: NIST SP 800-88 Rev. 2 §3.1.1 明確指出，SSD 的備用儲存單元與 Wear Leveling，可能使一般覆寫方式無法觸及所有曾儲存敏感資訊的實體區域。
所以，在真正的資料清理決策中，不能只依照磁碟容量或覆寫次數選擇方法，而必須考慮儲存媒體的控制器、支援指令、韌體及實際清理保證。
5. Cryptographic Erase：只要讓金鑰失效，就可以安全清理嗎？
這是一個非常重要的概念。
假設你有一台使用可信全碟加密的 SSD。
所有敏感資料都在寫入媒體前加密，對應金鑰受到適當保護。
當需要清理資料時，可以在符合條件的情況下，透過安全清除必要金鑰的方式，使媒體上的密文無法再被解密。
這就是 Cryptographic Erase（CE，加密清除）。
但它至少必須滿足以下條件：

items: 目標敏感資料沒有先前以未加密形式殘留於該媒體。
加密演算法、金鑰產生與實作具有足夠的可信度。
相關金鑰的所有可用副本均受到適當處置。
不存在可重新取得相同解密能力的金鑰備份或託管途徑。
清理程序經過驗證，且其結果足以支持風險判斷。

body.text: NIST SP 800-88 Rev. 2 §3.2.2–3.2.4 直接討論上述先決條件，並參照 ISO/IEC 27040 的儲存安全與金鑰管理要求。
要特別理解：
Cryptographic Erase 不代表把硬碟中的所有位元都變成零。
它的保護依據是：原有密文仍可能存在，但組織已確實消除取得必要解密能力的可行途徑。
如果原始資料曾經以明文存放，或金鑰在其他地方仍能取得，就不能只根據一個「刪除金鑰成功」訊息，斷言資料清理已經完成。

sections.heading: 八、C23｜File Deletion：為什麼刪除檔案不等於清理資料？

body.text: 1. 檔案系統不是單純把資料放在資料夾裡
想像一家圖書館。
一本書放在第 5 排第 20 格，而圖書館的目錄記錄了這本書的位置。
如果管理員將目錄紀錄刪除：
「系統現在查不到這本書。」
但實體書籍是否仍然放在架上？
可能仍然存在。
很多傳統檔案系統的刪除行為與此相似。
作業系統可能解除檔名與儲存資料之間的參照關係，並將相應空間標記為可重新使用，卻不一定立即覆寫實際資料內容。
MITRE ATT&CK 的 T1485（Data Destruction）也指出，常見的 rm、del 等檔案刪除指令，往往只是移除檔案參照，而不會確保所有原始資料內容都遭到抹除。
2. 必須區分四種不同操作

headers: 是否足以證明安全清理
rows: 移除檔案系統中的檔案參照或使檔案不可見
重新初始化部分檔案系統結構
嘗試以新資料取代既有儲存內容
需依媒體、介面及清理目標判斷
使用經核准且適用的 Clear、Purge 或 Destroy 方法

body.text: 這裡還有一個進階細節：現代 SSD 可能透過 TRIM 與背景回收程序，讓被刪除資料在某些情況下難以透過一般介面還原。
但這不是所有 SSD 的固定行為，也不能因此將「刪除檔案」直接等同於經驗證的媒體清理程序。
3. 美國矽谷：雲端資料刪除比本機硬碟更複雜
假設一家矽谷 SaaS 公司讓客戶透過網站刪除專案。
客戶按下 Delete 後，資料可能從網站消失。
但它先前可能分散在：

items: 主要資料庫。
Read Replica（讀取複本）。
Object Storage（物件儲存）。
Backup（備份）。
Snapshot（快照）。
Log（系統日誌）。
Cache（快取）。

body.text: 這些是不同的資料實體或副本，不一定同步消失。
因此，雲端資料清理應回答：
「我們究竟刪掉了哪一份資料？是否存在其他副本？各副本何時依法或依政策到期？如何驗證後續處置？」
NIST SP 800-88 Rev. 2 的 Executive Summary 特別指出，現代資料會經過多個組織、系統與儲存媒體，資料清理責任必須涵蓋分散式與雲端環境。
4. 臺美法律中的資料刪除義務
臺灣：《個人資料保護法》第 11 條
個人資料蒐集的特定目的消失或期限屆滿時，原則上應主動或依當事人請求刪除、停止處理或利用，但條文也規定執行職務、業務必要等例外。
美國加州：California Civil Code §1798.81
適用的企業對不再保留、且含有個人資訊的客戶紀錄，須採取合理的處置措施，例如碎毀、抹除或以其他方式使資訊無法閱讀或理解。
兩者說明的是法律上的資料處理與處置責任；具體採用什麼儲存清理技術，仍要依資料性質、媒體類型和適用技術要求選擇。
C23 核心：檔案不可見、檔案系統顯示空間已釋放、資料實際不可復原，是三件不同的事。

sections.heading: 九、C24｜Hardware Recycling、Archiving 與 Sanitization：為什麼三者不能混為一談？

body.text: 這是把 C22、C23 延伸到企業資產管理的最後一個觀念。
1. 三個操作的目的根本不同
Recycling（回收） 的主要目的，是將不再使用的設備或材料重新利用。
Archiving（封存／歸檔） 的目的，是在特定期間內保留紀錄，供稽核、業務、法律或研究需要。
Sanitization（資料清理） 的目的，是防止目標資料在媒體處置或再利用過程中遭到不當還原或揭露。

rows: 不應因回收而不當殘留敏感資料
合法且必要的紀錄保存
是，依適用保存期限與政策
消除殘留資料暴露風險
清理目標資料不應仍可被不當還原

body.text: 特別注意：封存不是刪除，回收也不是清理。
2. 真正的金融監理案例：設備報廢與資產清冊缺失
金管會檢查局公開的《113 年度上半年票券金融公司主要檢查缺失》第 8 頁記載了實際資安缺失類型：
檢查發現部分資訊儲存設備報廢時，沒有實施適當的資料清理或實體破壞；另有從報廢主機拆下的硬碟，安裝到其他主機繼續使用，卻未納入財產清冊。
金管會檢查局要求依內部規範進行適當的清理或銷毀，並對再利用設備妥善保管及列入資產清冊。
這裡有兩個不同的控制失效：

items: 資料保護失效： 報廢媒體仍可能保存敏感資訊。
資產治理失效： 組織無法完整追蹤硬碟的去向與再利用狀態。

body.text: 這份文件針對的是票券金融公司，屬於金管會公開的檢查缺失與改善指引，不應直接視為所有銀行共通的逐字作業條文；但對金融機構的資訊資產治理極具參考價值。
3. 臺灣半導體：舊設備轉售前應做什麼？
假設一家半導體公司準備處分老舊製造設備，設備內包含：

items: 設備維護電腦的 SSD。
製程參數與操作日誌。
控制器的非揮發性記憶體。
維修人員儲存的設定與診斷資料。

body.text: 即使主要 SSD 已清理，也不能直接推定所有設備元件都不再保存敏感資訊。
NIST SP 800-88 Rev. 2 第 4 章特別要求組織識別儲存媒體、資料保護等級、媒體再利用方式及清理需求。附錄 B 亦列出評估儲存設備特性時應注意的問題。
而《營業秘密法》第 2 條把合理保密措施列為營業秘密成立的必要要件之一。因此，對可能含有先進製程、配方或設計資訊的媒體，清理和資產管控不只是 IT 例行工作，也有助於維持營業秘密保護制度。
4. 最重要的取捨：資料是否應該先保留？
不能因為 Purge 很安全，就對所有舊資料立即執行 Purge。
假設某銀行有一份交易資料，依適用法律或監理規定仍有保存義務。
即使業務部門認為該資料「不再常用」，也不代表可以直接銷毀。
實務上應先確認：

items: 法律與合約是否要求繼續保存？
是否存在稽核、爭議處理或其他合法保存需求？
資料是否已超過適用的保存期限？
是否還有其他複本或備份？
決定清理後，如何留下不包含原始敏感內容的必要證據？

body.text: 這是資料治理的核心矛盾：
保存太久，會增加資料暴露風險；過早銷毀，則可能違反保存義務，並損害稽核、調查與營運需求。
因此資料生命週期應由資料擁有者、法遵、資安及資產管理職責共同協調，而非由執行刪除指令的人單獨決定。

sections.heading: 十、實務深化：如何建立可稽核的資料清理程序？

body.text: 理解 C22–C24 後，我們應該進一步把知識轉換成企業能實際執行的程序。
1. 六個階段的資料清理治理模型

body.name: sanitizationprogram
body.caption: 媒體清理治理的六步驟
body.description: 確認保留義務、執行品質與證據，才可完成結案。

items.title: 1｜Identify — 辨識
items.body: 確認媒體序號、擁有者、資料類別、敏感度及所有已知資料副本。

items.title: 2｜Authorize — 授權
items.body: 確認資料保存期限、法律義務、Legal Hold（法律保留）及核准人員。

items.title: 3｜Select — 選擇
items.body: 根據媒體技術、敏感程度、復原威脅及再利用需求，決定 Clear、Purge 或 Destroy。

items.title: 4｜Execute — 執行
items.body: 使用核准工具與程序，記錄操作人員、設備識別資訊及執行結果。

items.title: 5｜Verify / Validate — 確認
items.body: 先確認操作是否成功完成，再判斷該結果是否符合資料機密性所需的保護程度。

items.title: 6｜Document — 紀錄與結案
items.body: 保存清理證明、覆核與核准紀錄，決定媒體可否釋出、再使用或報廢。

body.text: 這個六階段流程是根據 NIST SP 800-88 Rev. 2 第 4 章的 Media Sanitization Program 整理出的實務模型。
2. Verification 與 Validation 的區別
這是本章進一步深化時最值得掌握的細節。
假設你對一台 SSD 執行資料清理指令。
工具回報：
Sanitization completed successfully
這代表什麼？
它只能支持「執行結果已完成」這一層面的判斷，不足以單獨證明清理方法對目標資料已達到所需的保護程度。
NIST SP 800-88 Rev. 2 §4.5 明確區分：

rows: 資料是否達到所需的清理保證？
執行狀態、錯誤、異常、設備狀況
結果是否符合資料敏感度、媒體與風險要求
調查、重新執行或更換方法
拒絕接受結果，補強或提升清理方法

body.text: 例如，拿消磁設備對 SSD 執行操作，設備可能回報操作正常完成，但 SSD 並不依賴磁性儲存資料，因此該操作無法達到預期的清理目標。
這正是 NIST 在 §4.5.2 提出的錯誤清理方法案例。
所以，系統顯示 Success，與安全目標真正達成，不是同一個命題。
這也和 C17 的安全控制概念一致：部署控制、執行控制、驗證控制有效性，是三個不同的工程活動。

sections.heading: 十一、跨產業整合：三種實務情境應如何設計？

rows: 機房與製造設備區域授權
資料中心與設備庫存保護
機房、設備與存取權限管理
雲端網路邊界及 API 防護
交易系統與外部連線控制
設備端點防護、供應商惡意程式風險
保護製程與客戶設計資料
報廢設備及儲存元件清理
雲端資料刪除、SSD 再利用
儲存設備報廢及再利用管控
營業秘密法、適用合約與 SEMI 標準
適用的加州法律及工程標準
金管會法規、銀行公會規範與監理檢查

body.text: 這些措施應依產業風險配置，不能假定所有公司都必須採用完全相同的控制。
各產業最有代表性的依據
臺灣半導體科技業
《營業秘密法》第 2 條提供營業秘密保護的法律基礎。SEMI E187、E188 則可作為設備資安及惡意程式防護的技術基礎。NIST SP 800-82 Rev. 3 可補充 OT 安全設計方法。SEMI 標準的具體遵循義務還須依採購合約、客戶要求與相關制度確認。
美國矽谷科技業
California Civil Code §1798.81 規範適用企業對不再保留的客戶個人資訊紀錄採取合理處置措施。NIST SP 800-53 的 MP-6 與 SP 800-88 Rev. 2 則可協助工程團隊選擇、實施及驗證媒體清理控制。前者是法律，後兩者是技術與管理依據。
臺灣金融機構
《金融控股公司及銀行業內部控制及稽核制度實施辦法》第 12、25 條提供內部控制及資訊安全制度要求。金管會檢查局公開的儲存設備報廢缺失，則顯示清理程序、設備再利用及資產清冊是實際的監理關注事項。

sections.heading: 十二、研究深化：安全清理與惡意資料破壞有什麼差別？

body.text: 這裡可以利用 MITRE ATT&CK 建立另一個重要連結。
MITRE ATT&CK T1485（Data Destruction）描述攻擊者破壞資料，影響系統與服務可用性的技術行為。
T1490（Inhibit System Recovery）則描述攻擊者透過破壞或移除備份、復原機制，阻礙系統恢復運作。
兩者與 Media Sanitization 看起來都可能涉及資料刪除，但目的相反：

rows: 防止不再需要的敏感資料外洩
破壞資料或系統可用性
攻擊者選擇的破壞目標
達成預期的資料生命週期處置
可能導致非預期資料損失與中斷

body.text: 這說明：不能僅從指令或工具名稱判斷一項操作的安全性質，還必須分析其授權、目的、執行脈絡與造成的結果。

sections.heading: 十三、這八個觀念應該如何記憶？

body.text: 建議用以下八個核心問題，取代死背名詞。

rows: 控制如何實施、發揮什麼功能、保護什麼目標？
如何防止未授權者實體接觸資產？
哪些網路連線應該允許或拒絕？
如何預防、偵測與處理惡意程式？
如何使未持有必要金鑰者難以理解資料？
如何使先進資料復原方法不可行？
刪除檔案參照是否真的移除了資料？
資料應保留、清理，還是設備應報廢回收？

body.text: 這八項又可以濃縮成兩個思考軸線：
控制正在使用的資產：C17–C21。控制資料生命週期終點：C22–C24。

sections.heading: 十四、理解檢查：整合型實務案例

body.text: 以下先不公布答案。請試著用本章概念及規範依據獨立推理。
案例：半導體企業的設備退役與銀行資料安全
一家臺灣半導體設備供應商，準備淘汰一批工廠伺服器，並將其中可用的 SSD 交給外部設備商回收。
同時，該企業使用一家美國矽谷公司的 SaaS 平台保存維修紀錄，並向臺灣銀行申請設備融資。
企業資安主管發現下列情況：
A. 工廠機房已經配置防火牆與防毒軟體，但是沒有進出管制，任何員工都可以接觸伺服器。
B. 某伺服器 SSD 已經快速格式化，IT 人員認為裡面的客戶機密資料已經完全消失。
C. 另一台 SSD 使用全碟加密，但企業無法確認解密金鑰是否還有備份。
D. SaaS 供應商已從正式資料庫刪除企業的維修資料，但仍可能存在備份及快照。
E. 外部回收商提供一份清理完成報告，內容只有「清除成功」，沒有設備序號、清理方法、執行結果或覆核紀錄。
請回答：
1. 安全控制分類： A 缺少哪一類控制？應該怎麼補強？為什麼防火牆與防毒無法替代？
2. 資料清理方法： B 的快速格式化與 NIST 的 Clear、Purge 有什麼差別？若要再利用 SSD，應如何選擇清理方法？
3. 加密清除： 對 C 而言，使用 Cryptographic Erase 前必須先驗證哪些條件？為什麼金鑰備份會改變結論？
4. 資料生命週期： 對 D 而言，如何同時處理資料清理要求、必要保存期限與分散式備份？
5. 稽核與證據： 對 E 而言，應補齊哪些證據才能支持 Verification 與 Validation？應援引 NIST SP 800-88 Rev. 2 哪些章節？
6. 產業規範： 如果你要向臺灣半導體客戶、美國 SaaS 業者及金管會監理下的銀行說明這套制度，應分別援引哪些法律、標準或監理依據？它們哪些具有法律約束力，哪些屬於技術標準或企業政策？
完成這六題後，便能檢查自己是否真正掌握 C17–C24 的分類、控制機制、儲存技術、治理程序與產業適用性，而不是僅能辨認 CEH 選項中的名詞。

en.title: CEH M01 | C17–C24: Security controls and media sanitization

sections.heading: Core conclusion: Control information-security risk throughout use and eliminate residual exposure at the end of the data lifecycle

body.text: CEH v13 · M01-06 Security controls and defense in depth · Eight core concepts
This unit addresses two core questions:
First, how do we protect systems and data still in use? Understand security controls, including physical and technical controls, firewalls, antivirus and encryption.
Second, when data is no longer needed, how do we prevent its recovery? This involves media sanitization, purge, ordinary file deletion, storage-media recycling and retention policy.
These questions concern different stages of the same lifecycle:

body.name: lifecyclecontrols
body.caption: Data lifecycle and sanitization
body.description: Choose methods using data risk, media capabilities and verified outcomes.

items.title: Data in use
items.body: Prevent unauthorized access, tampering and service disruption.

items.title: Storage, backups and archives
items.body: Control who can access data, how it is retained and for how long.

items.title: End of lifecycle
items.body: Select appropriate disposition, such as Clear, Purge or Destroy.

items.title: Verification and evidence
items.body: Verify sanitization and preserve evidence so subsequent reuse, disposal or outsourced recycling meets risk requirements.

body.text: NIST published SP 800-88 Revision 2 on September 26, 2025, superseding Revision 1 from 2014. The revision emphasizes an organization-wide media sanitization program, confidence in sanitization techniques and verification, rather than merely operating a deletion tool.
The teaching retains CEH terminology and explains its technical meaning using the current NIST standard.

sections.heading: 1. Complete knowledge map: C17–C24

body.text: The supplied manuscript places these eight concepts under M01-06. C17–C21 cover control classification and specific controls; C22–C24 distinguish sanitization from other disposition actions. The course attachment cited by the manuscript marks the last three as subitems awaiting confirmation; this does not establish separate official lessons.

rows: How should controls be classified and selected?
What can physical security and environmental protection prevent?
How does a firewall control network traffic?
How does antivirus identify and block malware?
Which security properties can encryption protect?
How can sanitization make advanced recovery infeasible?
Why does deleting a file not necessarily remove its actual data?
How do hardware recycling, archiving and sanitization differ?

body.text: The examples use engineering situations in three real industries: Taiwan semiconductor manufacturing, Silicon Valley cloud technology and Taiwan financial institutions supervised by the FSC. NIST, OWASP and MITRE ATT&CK support the technical explanations; applicable laws, industry standards and self-regulatory rules establish the practical requirements.

sections.heading: 2. C17 | Security Controls: What is a security control?

body.text: 1. Plain-language explanation: Manage risk rather than eliminate every risk
Suppose you manage cybersecurity at an advanced wafer fab.
The company has three concerns:

items: An external attacker compromises the manufacturing management system over the network.
An unauthorized person enters an equipment server room.
A third party recovers process data from a retired hard drive.

body.text: What would you do?
Use firewalls, network segmentation and access controls for the first concern; access restrictions and guards for the second; sanitization and disposal management for the third.
These are all security controls.
A control may be personnel, policy, equipment, a workflow or a technical mechanism, as well as software.

The NIST SP 800-53 Rev. 5 catalog includes Access Control (AC), Physical and Environmental Protection (PE), System and Communications Protection (SC) and Media Protection (MP) families. Its maintenance release has reached Release 5.2.0.
2. Understand three dimensions of classification together
This is the chapter's first core concept.

body.name: controlaxes
body.caption: Three axes for classifying controls
body.description: The axes can describe the same control; they are not sequential steps. A control may serve preventive, detective and other functions at once; the axes are not mutually exclusive.

items.title: A | Implementation
items.body: Administrative: policies, rules, people and procedures / Technical: software, systems, networks and cryptography / Physical: entry controls, guards, facilities and physical equipment

items.title: B | Function
items.body: Preventive: reduce the likelihood of incidents / Detective: discover incidents or anomalies / Corrective: fix identified problems / Recovery: restore necessary capabilities / Deterrent: reduce motivation to act / Compensating: replace or supplement other controls

items.title: C | Protection objectives
items.body: Confidentiality, integrity and availability (CIA), plus identity, traceability and privacy requirements where applicable.

body.text: These dimensions can intersect; they are not three mutually exclusive classifications. A control may also perform prevention, detection and other functions together.
3. A control can perform several functions

rows: Data confidentiality; suitable modes also verify integrity

body.text: The final row illustrates why classification must follow the actual mechanism.
Sanitizing encryption keys is a logical or technical operation; physically shredding storage chips is physical disposition. Both may sanitize media while using different forms of control.
4. Defense in Depth: Why use several layers?
Suppose a semiconductor company deploys only a firewall.
If an employee copies confidential data directly to a USB drive, the firewall may never observe the action.
Now suppose the company has only server-room guards.
If an attacker exploits an API vulnerability through an intentionally available HTTPS service, the guards cannot directly stop it.
This is why defense in depth is needed.

body.name: defenselayers
body.caption: Four layers of defense in depth
body.description: Outer layers contain inner layers; multiple controls protect core assets. Multiple layers aim to prevent one failed control from causing unacceptable consequences; each control must still be verified for effectiveness.

items.title: Physical and environmental
items.body: Facility access and environmental protection

items.title: Network segmentation and traffic
items.body: Segments, boundaries and traffic controls

items.title: Endpoint and identity
items.body: Endpoint protection, accounts and privileges

items.title: Critical data and systems
items.body: Encryption, authentication, backups and integrity

body.text: C17 takeaway: Ask how the control is implemented, what functions it performs and which security objective it protects.

sections.heading: 3. C18 | Physical Controls: Why is a guard an information-security control?

body.text: 1. A secure network still leaves physical assets exposed to contact
Suppose a bank has a highly protected database.
The system has a firewall, encryption and multifactor authentication.
But the server-room door is unlocked: visitors can enter, remove backup media or touch servers.
The missing protection here is physical controls, rather than another encryption algorithm.
Physical security controls use people, facilities and physical mechanisms to prevent unauthorized contact with important assets.
2. Why is a security guard a physical control?
Guards restrict physical access through on-site identity checks, patrols, monitoring and entry controls.

NIST SP 800-53 Rev. 5 PE-3 (Physical Access Control) explicitly includes guards among facility-access enforcement mechanisms; PE-6 (Monitoring Physical Access) addresses monitoring physical access and responding to incidents.
A guard is a person, but the main control performed in this classification is physical security rather than administrative control.
This distinction is relevant to CEH control-classification questions.
3. Taiwan semiconductor practice: Server rooms and manufacturing-equipment areas
Suppose a wafer fab has three kinds of space:

rows: Basic entry control and visitor registration
Authorized personnel only, locked racks and access records
Maintenance authorization, physical access restrictions and on-site safety procedures

body.text: This is an example designed around asset risk.
NIST SP 800-82 Rev. 3 emphasizes the relationship between physical processes, safety and availability when selecting OT security controls.
Entry controls and emergency evacuation therefore need coordinated design in manufacturing environments; cybersecurity controls must preserve personnel safety.
4. Relationship to Taiwan financial supervision

Article 12 of Taiwan's Regulations Governing the Implementation of Internal Control and Audit Systems by Financial Holding Companies and Banking Industries requires internal controls to cover information management and customer-data confidentiality. Article 25 requires information-security systems to maintain confidentiality, integrity and availability.

Entry controls, visitor management and server-room protection can help financial institutions meet those objectives. These provisions do not require every bank to adopt an identical guard-staffing arrangement.
C18 takeaway: Guards, entry controls, fences and rack locks are principally physical security controls; firewalls and encryption are technical controls.

sections.heading: 4. C19 | Firewall: What does a firewall protect?

body.text: 1. A firewall is a checkpoint for network traffic
Suppose a wafer fab has two networks:

items: IT Network: Corporate office and general information systems.
OT Network: Manufacturing equipment and factory-control systems.

body.text: The company does not want office computers to connect freely to manufacturing equipment.
It therefore establishes a firewall between the networks.

body.name: firewallpolicy
body.caption: IT/OT firewall boundary
body.description: Only approved policy-compliant traffic passes; Deny means blocked.

items.title: IT network
items.body: Enterprise office endpoints and general information systems.

items.title: Firewall
items.body: Check source, destination and service rules

items.title: OT network
items.body: Manufacturing equipment and factory operational control systems.

items.title: Allow | Approved management
items.body: Permit management connections that match policy.

items.title: Deny | Unauthorized direct access
items.body: Block unapproved direct connections.

body.text: A firewall decides which connections may pass by applying rules to traffic characteristics.
Common criteria include source and destination IP addresses, protocol, port and connection state. More advanced products also inspect application-layer traffic.
NIST SP 800-53 SC-7 (Boundary Protection) is an important system-boundary control. OT segmentation design can also draw on NIST SP 800-82 Rev. 3.
2. A firewall has limits
Imagine a Silicon Valley SaaS company that permits users to access its API over HTTPS.
An attacker uses an ordinary connection but exploits an API authorization flaw to read another user's data.
The firewall may permit HTTPS because the connection complies with network policy.
The actual flaw is in the application's authorization logic.
Additional protections include:

items: Network Firewall: Protect network and connection boundaries.
WAF (Web Application Firewall): Inspect suspicious patterns in HTTP requests.
Application Authorization: Backend code checks a user's permission for a specific record or function.

body.text: OWASP WSTG explains that a WAF can help block common attacks such as SQL injection and XSS, while providing limited protection against access-control and business-logic flaws.
3. How do engineers verify a firewall?
Asking whether a firewall is installed is insufficient.
Ask these questions:

items: Which connections should be allowed, and which denied?
Do the actual rules grant only the minimum necessary access?
Can any connection bypass the intended network path?
Are rules reviewed regularly and changes recorded?
Are abnormal connections monitored and handled?

body.text: C19 takeaway: A firewall is a technical control that principally provides preventive traffic enforcement and may also provide monitoring and logs. It cannot replace authorization inside an application.

sections.heading: 5. C20 | Antivirus: How does antivirus recognize a problematic program?

body.text: 1. Antivirus does more than match virus names
Suppose a semiconductor-equipment technician connects a USB device to a maintenance computer.
A seemingly normal utility on the device actually contains malware.
Antivirus may identify the problem using several techniques.

rows: Unknown variants may lack a matching signature
Analyze suspicious structure or behavioral features
Some malicious activity may already have occurred
Collect endpoint activity, investigate and respond
Requires correct deployment, permissions and ongoing monitoring

body.text: Several mechanisms may coexist in one product.
NIST SP 800-53 SI-3 (Malicious Code Protection) is the corresponding malware-protection control.
2. Semiconductor requirements: Security updates may affect equipment
Employee computers may receive relatively frequent security updates.
However, updating endpoint-protection components on equipment with extensively validated control software may affect drivers, performance or availability.
Office-computer update practices therefore require adaptation before use across manufacturing equipment.
Relevant SEMI industry standards:

SEMI E187, Specification for Cybersecurity of Fab Equipment, establishes baseline cybersecurity requirements for semiconductor manufacturing equipment, including operating systems, network security, endpoint protection and logging.
SEMI E188, Specification for Malware Free Equipment Integration, focuses on reducing the introduction and spread of malware during equipment delivery and support.
Their purposes differ: E187 emphasizes the equipment cybersecurity baseline; E188 emphasizes malware propagation during integration and support.
In 2026, SEMI announced a major revision direction for a tiered E187 security framework. A revision plan does not establish that new requirements already apply to all existing equipment.
3. Antivirus is not a sanitization tool
Connect this distinction to C22–C24.
Suppose a bank is retiring a server with up-to-date antivirus that detects no malware.
This does not establish that customer data on the server has been safely sanitized.
The reason is:
Antivirus manages malware risk; media sanitization manages the confidentiality risk of residual data.
The first cannot replace the second.
C20 takeaway: Antivirus is a technical control that may prevent, detect and partly respond to malware. Detecting no malware does not establish the absence of other security risks.

sections.heading: 6. C21 | Encryption: What can encryption solve, and where are its limits?

body.text: 1. Encryption makes data difficult to understand without the necessary key
Suppose a Silicon Valley technology company stores customers' important business data in the cloud.
If the data is plaintext, unauthorized access to storage may directly expose its content.
With suitable encryption, obtaining the ciphertext without the decryption key makes recovering its content difficult.
The basic encryption model is:
C = E_K(P)
P = D_K(C)
Here:

items: P: Plaintext.
C: Ciphertext.
K: The key needed for encryption and decryption in this symmetric model.
E and D: Encryption and decryption algorithms.

body.text: 2. Encryption principally protects confidentiality and can include integrity protection
This distinction is another common source of confusion.
Encryption in a mode without authentication does not necessarily prevent an attacker from modifying ciphertext undetected.
Modern systems often use Authenticated Encryption with Associated Data (AEAD), such as AES-GCM.
AEAD can provide confidentiality and data-integrity verification together. It does not automatically resolve business authorization, stolen keys or attribution of a user's identity.
OWASP's Cryptographic Storage Cheat Sheet recommends established cryptographic libraries, suitable algorithms and secure key management instead of inventing a cryptographic mechanism.
3. Three data states require different protection designs

rows: Memory and execution-environment protection; confidential computing in suitable cases

body.text: 4. Why does key management matter so much?
Suppose a semiconductor company encrypts all customer-design files but places the decryption key in a publicly accessible configuration file on the same server.
An attacker obtains the files and the key together.
Encryption is present, yet may fail to deliver its intended protection.

OWASP recommends managing key generation, storage, rotation, deactivation and destruction according to the system design. Suitable architectures separate data-encryption keys (DEKs) from key-encryption keys (KEKs).
A further question follows:
If the data is encrypted, does deleting its decryption key amount to sanitizing the data?
This is central to C22. The answer depends on keys, the encryption implementation, data copies and sanitization conditions; the presence of encryption alone does not settle it.

sections.heading: 7. C22 | Purge: What is effective media sanitization?

body.text: This part of C17–C24 warrants close attention to technical details.
1. Data may still exist when it is no longer visible
Suppose a Taiwan semiconductor company plans to give a five-year-old server to an equipment recycler.
An IT employee says:
“I formatted the drive, and all the files are gone.”
Does that establish that the drive is safe?
Not necessarily.
A file's visibility in the operating system and the existence of recoverable data on the media are separate questions.
The question that matters is:
If the next holder of the media has professional forensic equipment, time and technical expertise, can they still recover the original confidential data?
Media sanitization addresses this problem.
2. NIST SP 800-88 Rev. 2: Clear, Purge and Destroy
Section 3.1 of NIST SP 800-88 Rev. 2 defines three sanitization methods.

body.name: sanitizationmethods
body.caption: Clear / Purge / Destroy comparison
body.description: Choose based on sensitivity, media and intended use; these are not mandatory sequential stages.

items.title: Clear | §3.1.1
items.body: Goal: resist simple, non-invasive data recovery. Apply appropriate logical sanitization to user-accessible storage. Example: overwrite user-addressable data through standard read/write interfaces on suitable media.

items.title: Purge | §3.1.2
items.body: Goal: make recovery of target data infeasible even with advanced laboratory techniques. Use logical or physical techniques appropriate to the media, potentially preserving reuse. Examples: qualifying device sanitization commands and Cryptographic Erase.

items.title: Destroy | §3.1.3
items.body: Goal: make recovery with advanced laboratory techniques infeasible and render the media unable to store data. Use media-appropriate physical destruction. Examples: media shredding to suitable specifications, disintegration or other approved destruction techniques.

body.text: The distinction concerns the threat model and achievable sanitization assurance, rather than merely one, three or seven overwrite passes.
The revised NIST guidance requires techniques suited to actual media characteristics, drawing on IEEE 2883, relevant NSA specifications or organization-approved standards.
3. Why does Purge not mean mathematically impossible recovery forever?
The supplied manuscript explicitly flags this ambiguity in the original question's wording.

The manuscript reports absolute wording such as “impossible even with laboratory-grade tools” in the original question; its complete text has not been independently checked here. The standard instead concerns making recovery infeasible under specified technical and resource conditions.
Distinguish:

items: Logical impossibility: An outcome is impossible in principle.
Computational infeasibility: An outcome cannot feasibly be achieved with realistically available time, resources and technical capability.
Operational assurance: A trusted procedure has been followed and sufficient evidence supports the sanitization outcome.

body.text: NIST uses risk- and capability-based criteria. It does not promise an absolute guarantee for every medium against all future technology.
4. Why does conventional overwriting not apply uniformly to SSDs?
Begin with the difference between HDDs and SSDs.
Conventional HDDs principally store data magnetically.
SSDs use flash memory and a controller that manages physical data locations, wear leveling and overprovisioned storage.
When the operating system requests a write to a logical address, the SSD controller may write to a different physical location rather than overwrite the original cell directly.

body.name: ssdremapping
body.caption: SSD logical overwrite and FTL remapping
body.description: Old Page A and new Page B are concurrent remapping outcomes, not an A-to-B sequence. Actual behavior depends on the controller, firmware and storage technology; not every overwrite produces the same result.

items.title: Operating system
items.body: Requests an overwrite of logical block LBA 100.

items.title: SSD controller / FTL
items.body: Maps logical addresses to physical flash memory.

items.title: Old Page A
items.body: Original physical storage page: old data may not yet have been physically erased.

items.title: New Page B
items.body: New physical storage page: the new data write has completed.

body.text: NIST SP 800-88 Rev. 2 §3.1.1 explains that spare cells and wear leveling may prevent ordinary overwriting from reaching every physical area that previously held sensitive information.
A sanitization decision therefore must consider the media controller, supported commands, firmware and actual assurance, rather than selecting a method solely by capacity or overwrite-pass count.
5. Cryptographic Erase: Does disabling a key safely sanitize data?
This concept requires careful conditions.
Suppose an SSD uses trusted full-disk encryption.
All sensitive data is encrypted before being written, and the relevant keys are properly protected.
When sanitization is needed and the necessary conditions hold, securely sanitizing the required keys can make ciphertext on the media undecryptable.
This is Cryptographic Erase (CE).
At least these conditions must hold:

items: The target sensitive data has not previously remained on the media in unencrypted form.
Encryption algorithms, key generation and implementation provide sufficient confidence.
All available copies of the relevant keys receive appropriate disposition.
No key backup or escrow route can restore the same decryption capability.
The sanitization procedure is verified and its outcome supports the risk decision.

body.text: NIST SP 800-88 Rev. 2 §§3.2.2–3.2.4 discuss these prerequisites and refer to ISO/IEC 27040 for storage-security and key-management requirements.
Understand the following distinction:
Cryptographic Erase does not mean turning every bit on the drive into zero.
Its protection rests on eliminating feasible access to the necessary decryption capability even though the ciphertext may remain.
If plaintext existed previously or a key remains available elsewhere, a “key deletion successful” message alone cannot establish complete sanitization.

sections.heading: 8. C23 | File Deletion: Why is deletion different from sanitization?

body.text: 1. A file system does more than place data inside folders
Imagine a library.
A book sits at row 5, slot 20, and the catalog records its location.
If a librarian deletes that catalog entry:
“The system can no longer find the book.”
Is the physical book still on the shelf?
It may be.
Deletion in many traditional file systems is similar.
The operating system may unlink the filename from the stored data and mark its space reusable without immediately overwriting the actual content.
MITRE ATT&CK T1485 (Data Destruction) also notes that common commands such as rm and del often remove file references without ensuring that all original data content is erased.
2. Distinguish four different operations

rows: Remove a file-system reference or make a file invisible
Attempt to replace existing stored content with new data
Depends on media, interface and sanitization objective
Use an approved, applicable Clear, Purge or Destroy method

body.text: A further detail: On modern SSDs, TRIM and background garbage collection may make deleted data difficult to recover through ordinary interfaces in some circumstances.
This is not uniform behavior across all SSDs and does not equate file deletion with a verified sanitization procedure.
3. Silicon Valley: Cloud deletion is more complex than a local drive
Suppose a Silicon Valley SaaS company lets customers delete projects through a website.
After a customer selects Delete, the data may disappear from the site.
It may previously have been distributed across:

items: The primary database.
Read replicas.
Object storage.
Backups.
Snapshots.
System logs.
Caches.

body.text: These are different data objects or copies and need not disappear simultaneously.
Cloud sanitization must therefore answer:
Which copy did we delete? Do others exist? When does each copy expire under law or policy, and how will its subsequent disposition be verified?

The executive summary of NIST SP 800-88 Rev. 2 notes that modern data passes through several organizations, systems and storage media. Sanitization responsibilities must encompass distributed and cloud environments.
4. Data-deletion duties in Taiwan and US law
Taiwan: Personal Data Protection Act, Article 11

When a specific collection purpose disappears or a retention period expires, deletion or cessation of processing or use is generally required proactively or upon request. The article also provides exceptions, including necessity for official duties or business operations.
California: Civil Code §1798.81

Applicable businesses must take reasonable steps to dispose of customer records containing personal information that are no longer retained, such as shredding, erasing or otherwise making the information unreadable or undecipherable.

These establish legal responsibilities for processing and disposition. The specific storage-sanitization technique still depends on data characteristics, media type and applicable technical requirements.
C23 takeaway: A file becoming invisible, a file system reporting free space and data becoming unrecoverable are three separate states.

sections.heading: 9. C24 | Hardware Recycling, Archiving and Sanitization: Why distinguish them?

body.text: This final concept extends C22 and C23 to enterprise asset management.
1. The three operations have different purposes
Recycling reuses equipment or materials that are no longer needed.
Archiving retains records for a defined period to meet audit, business, legal or research needs.
Sanitization prevents inappropriate recovery or disclosure of target data during media disposition or reuse.

rows: Recycling must not leave sensitive data inappropriately exposed
Yes, according to applicable periods and policy
Target data should no longer be subject to inappropriate recovery

body.text: Archiving preserves data; recycling alone does not sanitize it.
2. A financial-supervision case: Disposal and asset-inventory deficiencies
Page 8 of the FSC Financial Examination Bureau's published Major Examination Deficiencies of Bills Finance Companies, First Half of ROC Year 113 (2024), records actual cybersecurity deficiency types:

Some storage devices were retired without appropriate sanitization or physical destruction. Drives removed from retired hosts were also installed in other hosts and reused without being entered in the property inventory.
The bureau calls for suitable sanitization or destruction under internal procedures and proper custody and inventory inclusion for reused equipment.
Two different controls have failed:

items: Data protection: Retired media may still contain sensitive information.
Asset governance: The organization cannot fully trace drive disposition and reuse.

body.text: This document concerns bills finance companies and provides published examination deficiencies and improvement guidance. It is not a verbatim operating rule for every bank, while still informing financial-institution information-asset governance.
3. Taiwan semiconductors: What precedes resale of old equipment?
Suppose a semiconductor company disposes of aging manufacturing equipment containing:

items: An SSD in the maintenance computer.
Process parameters and operating logs.
Nonvolatile controller memory.
Configuration and diagnostic data saved by technicians.

body.text: Sanitizing the main SSD does not establish that every component is free of sensitive information.

Chapter 4 of NIST SP 800-88 Rev. 2 requires identifying storage media, protection levels, reuse plans and sanitization needs. Appendix B also provides questions for assessing storage-device characteristics.

Article 2 of Taiwan's Trade Secrets Act includes reasonable confidentiality measures among the prerequisites for trade-secret protection. Sanitization and asset controls for media containing advanced processes, recipes or design information therefore also support the trade-secret protection program.
4. The retention decision comes first
The strength of Purge does not authorize immediately purging all old data.
Suppose a bank still has a legal or supervisory duty to retain transaction records.
A business unit's view that the records are rarely used does not authorize their destruction.
First establish:

items: Do laws or contracts require continued retention?
Do audit, dispute-resolution or other lawful retention needs exist?
Has the applicable retention period expired?
Are there other copies or backups?
After sanitization is approved, how can necessary evidence be retained without retaining the original sensitive content?

body.text: This creates a central data-governance tradeoff:
Overretention increases exposure; premature destruction may breach retention duties and harm audits, investigations and operations.
Data owners, compliance, security and asset-management roles must therefore coordinate lifecycle decisions, rather than leaving them solely to the person issuing a deletion command.

sections.heading: 10. Practice: Build an auditable sanitization procedure

body.text: Turn the C22–C24 concepts into a procedure an enterprise can execute.
1. A six-stage sanitization-governance model

body.name: sanitizationprogram
body.caption: Six steps for sanitization governance
body.description: Closure requires retention review, verified execution and evidence.

items.title: 1 | Identify
items.body: Confirm the media serial number, owner, data categories, sensitivity and all known data copies.

items.title: 2 | Authorize
items.body: Confirm retention periods, legal obligations, legal holds and approving personnel.

items.title: 3 | Select
items.body: Choose Clear, Purge or Destroy based on media technology, sensitivity, recovery threats and reuse requirements.

items.title: 4 | Execute
items.body: Use approved tools and procedures; record operators, device identifiers and execution outcomes.

items.title: 5 | Verify and validate
items.body: First verify successful completion; then validate whether the result provides the protection required for data confidentiality.

items.title: 6 | Document and close
items.body: Retain sanitization certificates, review and approval records; decide whether the media may be released, reused or disposed of.

body.text: This six-stage practical model is synthesized from the media sanitization program in Chapter 4 of NIST SP 800-88 Rev. 2.
2. Verification versus validation
This distinction deserves close attention.
Suppose you run a sanitization command on an SSD.
The tool reports:
Sanitization completed successfully
What does that mean?
It supports the judgment that execution completed. Alone, it does not establish that the chosen method achieved the protection required for the target data.
NIST SP 800-88 Rev. 2 §4.5 distinguishes:

rows: Did the data attain the required sanitization assurance?
Status, errors, anomalies and device condition
Whether results meet sensitivity, media and risk requirements
Reject the outcome and strengthen or escalate the method

body.text: For example, a degausser may report normal completion when used on an SSD. Since an SSD does not store data magnetically, that operation cannot achieve the intended sanitization objective.
NIST uses this unsuitable-method example in §4.5.2.
A Success message and achievement of the security objective are separate propositions.
This matches C17: deploying a control, executing it and verifying its effectiveness are three different engineering activities.

sections.heading: 11. Cross-industry integration: Design for three practical settings

rows: Authorized access to server rooms and manufacturing areas
Equipment endpoint protection and supplier malware risk
Trade Secrets Act, applicable contracts and SEMI standards
Applicable California laws and engineering standards
FSC regulations, bankers' association rules and supervisory examinations

body.text: Allocate controls according to industry risk; do not assume every company must deploy identical measures.
Representative authorities for each industry
Taiwan semiconductor technology

Trade Secrets Act Article 2 provides the legal foundation for trade-secret protection. SEMI E187 and E188 provide technical foundations for equipment cybersecurity and malware protection, supplemented by NIST SP 800-82 Rev. 3 for OT design. Specific SEMI obligations depend on procurement contracts, customer requirements and applicable programs.
Silicon Valley technology

California Civil Code §1798.81 requires reasonable disposition of customer personal-information records no longer retained by applicable businesses. NIST SP 800-53 MP-6 and SP 800-88 Rev. 2 help engineers select, implement and verify media-sanitization controls. The first is law; the latter two provide technical and management guidance.
Taiwan financial institutions

Articles 12 and 25 of the Regulations Governing the Implementation of Internal Control and Audit Systems by Financial Holding Companies and Banking Industries establish internal-control and information-security requirements. Published FSC examination deficiencies show that sanitization procedures, reuse and asset inventories are actual supervisory concerns.

sections.heading: 12. Research connection: Authorized sanitization versus malicious destruction

body.text: MITRE ATT&CK provides a useful connection.
T1485 (Data Destruction) describes attackers destroying data to impair system and service availability.
T1490 (Inhibit System Recovery) describes destroying or removing backups and recovery mechanisms to obstruct restoration.
These actions and media sanitization may all involve deletion, while serving opposite purposes:

rows: Prevent disclosure of sensitive data no longer needed
Destructive targets selected by the attacker
Potential unintended data loss and disruption

body.text: Classify an operation using its authorization, purpose, context and effects, rather than merely its tool or command name.

sections.heading: 13. Remember the eight concepts through questions

body.text: Use these eight questions instead of memorizing terms alone.

rows: How is a control implemented, what does it do, and what objective does it protect?
How do we prevent unauthorized physical contact with assets?
Which connections should be allowed or denied?
How do we prevent, detect and handle malware?
How do we make data difficult to understand without the necessary key?
How do we make advanced recovery infeasible?
Does removing a file reference actually remove its data?
Should data be retained or sanitized, or equipment retired and recycled?

body.text: The eight concepts also form two lines of reasoning:
Protect assets in use: C17–C21. Govern the end of the data lifecycle: C22–C24.

sections.heading: 14. Understanding check: An integrated case

body.text: Answers are withheld. Reason independently using the concepts and cited authorities.
Case: Semiconductor-equipment retirement and bank data security
A Taiwan semiconductor-equipment supplier is retiring factory servers and plans to give reusable SSDs to an external equipment recycler.
It also stores maintenance records on a Silicon Valley SaaS platform and applies to a Taiwan bank for equipment financing.
Its security manager discovers:
A. The factory server room has a firewall and antivirus but no entry control; any employee can touch the servers.
B. A server SSD has been quick-formatted, and IT believes all confidential customer data has disappeared completely.
C. Another SSD uses full-disk encryption, but the enterprise cannot establish whether decryption-key backups remain.
D. The SaaS supplier deleted maintenance data from production, but backups and snapshots may remain.
E. The recycler's completion report says only “erasure successful,” without serial numbers, method, execution results or review records.
Answer these questions:
1. Control classification: Which control type is missing in A, how would you strengthen it, and why cannot a firewall and antivirus replace it?
2. Sanitization methods: How does B's quick format differ from NIST Clear and Purge? How should a method be selected if the SSD will be reused?
3. Cryptographic Erase: Which conditions must be verified before using CE in C, and why do key backups change the conclusion?
4. Data lifecycle: For D, how would you coordinate sanitization, required retention periods and distributed backups?
5. Audit evidence: Which evidence must E add to support verification and validation? Which sections of NIST SP 800-88 Rev. 2 apply?

6. Industry authorities: Which laws, standards or supervisory authorities would you cite for Taiwan semiconductor customers, US SaaS providers and FSC-supervised banks? Which are legally binding and which are technical standards or enterprise policy?
These six questions examine classification, mechanisms, storage technology, governance and industry applicability across C17–C24, beyond recognizing terms in CEH choices.
